h1: Baron Zotel Bangkok — a budget hotel near Vejthani Hospital on Lat Phrao Soi 117, Bang Kapi
intro: If you have a medical appointment at Vejthani Hospital or you are accompanying family for treatment and need somewhere affordable close by — Baron Zotel Bangkok sits on Lat Phrao Soi 117, just 1.2 km from Vejthani, reachable in under five minutes by taxi or car · what draws guests here is a combination of loft-style rooms with private balconies, free parking, and a complimentary 24-hour golf-cart shuttle from the quiet soi out to the main Lat Phrao road · the hotel has 58 rooms and scores 8.3/10 from 579 reviews on Trip.com, with particular praise going to the friendly English-speaking staff · rooms start from about THB 500–900 per night depending on room type and season.

body.html: Who is Baron Zotel Bangkok right for? — To put it plainly, Baron Zotel Bangkok works best for people who have a specific reason to be in this part of the city: visiting or accompanying patients at Vejthani Hospital, attending medical appointments, or working in the Bang Kapi and Lat Phrao area · it is not a design hotel in the heart of Sukhumvit, nor is it a few steps from a major BTS station · it is a small, quiet, fairly priced hotel whose location only makes sense once you understand what it is close to · real guest reviews consistently reflect this: the guests who are most satisfied are medical visitors and family members needing affordable accommodation near Vejthani, international patients who value the staff's strong English, and drivers who need free parking in a city where that is hard to find · on the other hand, if you are visiting Bangkok purely as a tourist and want to be near Sukhumvit, Siam, or Khao San Road, the location will feel inconvenient and the taxi fares back and forth will add up.

Location and getting around — The hotel is at 77 Soi Lat Phrao 117, Khlong Chan, Bang Kapi, in the eastern suburbs of Bangkok · the most important distance for most guests: Vejthani Hospital sits just 1.2 km away, on Soi Lat Phrao 111, a short taxi or car ride of under five minutes (walking takes about 15 minutes in the heat) · the hotel runs a free golf-cart shuttle around the clock, ferrying guests between the hotel and the main Lat Phrao road — useful because the property is set back in a quiet residential soi · the closest shopping is The Mall Bangkapi, a few minutes by car, good for restaurants, a supermarket, and everyday needs · for rail travel, the nearest station is MRT Yellow Line Bang Kapi (YL8), roughly 1.5 km away — to be honest, as several reviews note, the walking distance is closer to 20–25 minutes rather than the nine minutes the hotel advertises · the practical approach is to take the free golf-cart shuttle to the main road and then call a Grab · from Bang Kapi station you can ride the Yellow Line to Lat Phrao interchange (YL1) and connect to the Blue Line for Ratchada, Huai Khwang and Rama 9.
"Staff is very friendly and helpful, the room is spacious with a nice balcony. Location is perfect for visiting Vejthani Hospital — just a short ride away. Free parking was a big plus."

Rooms and design — Baron Zotel has 58 guest rooms fitted out in an industrial-loft aesthetic: exposed brick or raw concrete walls, a design touch that sets it apart from standard budget hotels of this price tier · every room comes with a private balcony, which draws consistent praise from guests — somewhere to sit in the morning or the cooler evening without leaving your floor · room fittings cover the essentials: air-conditioning, a 32-inch LCD TV with cable channels, fridge, free Wi-Fi, and an en-suite bathroom with hot shower · room categories are Superior (queen bed, balcony) and Deluxe (slightly larger, bigger balcony) · the majority of reviews describe rooms as clean and more spacious than expected at this price · honest caveats that appear more than once: some rooms have a slightly damp or musty smell in the bathroom, and the in-room lighting is on the dim side according to a few guests · a handful of reviewers also note the room photos online look somewhat better than the reality — worth calibrating expectations to a budget loft property rather than a four-star.

Facilities — For a 58-room budget hotel, the property covers the practical bases well · the headline amenities are free parking — genuinely valuable in Bangkok's east for anyone driving from the provinces — and the 24-hour complimentary golf-cart shuttle to the main road, which solves the deep-soi problem neatly · free Wi-Fi runs through the hotel and rooms, though a number of reviews flag that it can slow down in the evenings · one significant caveat: the hotel previously operated an Aladdin Rooftop Bar that featured in earlier promotional materials, but multiple recent reviews confirm it is no longer open — if a rooftop or bar facility matters to you, verify with the hotel before booking · breakfast is listed as available in some booking windows, but guests also report it was not running during their stay, so confirm this directly too · the 24-hour front desk is consistently praised; staff are described as proactive, warm, and notably capable in English — an important detail for international patients at Vejthani.
"The rooftop bar was listed but turned out to be closed. We were a bit disappointed. Room was clean and the balcony is a nice touch, but manage expectations about the advertised features."

Service — Service is where Baron Zotel consistently scores highest in verified reviews · on Trip.com, the service sub-score comes in at 8.8/10, the hotel's highest category score and a full half-point above the overall 8.3 · staff are described repeatedly as friendly, attentive, and importantly for an internationally-visited medical destination, fluent in English and patient with medical-visit inquiries · one thing to watch: a few reviews mention an undisclosed credit card surcharge added at check-in · it is worth asking directly about payment methods and any fees when you arrive to avoid surprises · the hotel also holds a 500 THB security deposit at check-in, refundable on check-out.

What real guests say (the good and the honest caveats) — Drawing from Trip.com, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor, the picture that emerges is a small hotel with clear strengths and equally clear limits · What guests praise: rooms that are cleaner and larger than the price suggests, private balconies on every room, friendly and helpful English-speaking staff, free parking, a free shuttle that solves the soi problem, a quiet and safe residential location, and a score-to-price ratio that feels fair for those coming to the area with a purpose · What guests flag: the rooftop bar is closed despite ongoing mentions online; Wi-Fi slows in the evenings; the MRT station is farther than the hotel claims (20–25 minutes on foot, not nine); some bathroom conditions are variable; and there are reports of an undisclosed credit card processing fee at the desk · overall, an 8.3 from 579 Trip.com reviews is a solid signal — guests who arrive knowing what the hotel is (a budget loft property for east Bangkok and Vejthani visitors) tend to leave satisfied.

Value and pricing — Superior rooms start from about THB 500–650 per night in regular periods, and Deluxe rooms run from roughly THB 700–900 (approximately USD 13–26 on international platforms, sometimes lower in quiet months) · compared to alternatives in the same corridor near Vejthani, Baron Zotel offers arguably the best combination of online review score, private balconies, free parking, and free shuttle in the budget bracket · the 500 THB refundable deposit is standard · prices vary meaningfully across platforms — comparing Agoda, Booking, and Trip.com before booking is worth the two minutes.

Before you book — what to know — A few things that make the stay smoother · First, ask about payment methods at check-in; clarify whether there is a card surcharge and what the deposit arrangement is · Second, do not rely on walking to the MRT Yellow Line — the real distance is closer to 20–25 minutes; use the free golf-cart to the main road and then Grab · Third, check with the hotel before arrival whether breakfast is being served during your dates · Fourth, if you have any issue with your room on arrival — smell, lighting, Wi-Fi — mention it at the desk; most reviews indicate staff respond quickly to requests · Fifth, if you are driving in, call ahead to confirm parking availability on your dates, as spaces are limited.

honestSummary: Baron Zotel Bangkok is a solid choice for people coming to the area for Vejthani Hospital or work in Bang Kapi: affordable, clean rooms with balconies, free parking, friendly English-speaking staff, and a free shuttle · be straight with yourself about the limits: the rooftop bar is closed, the MRT station is further than advertised, and if your goal is sightseeing around central Bangkok, the location works against you.
honestChecks: If you are visiting Bangkok as a tourist without a Vejthani-area reason — Soi Lat Phrao 117 is a long, expensive taxi ride from Sukhumvit, Siam, and most major sights → consider a hotel closer to the BTS network in a central area instead.

If you plan to use the MRT Yellow Line as your main transport — the real walking distance to Bang Kapi station is around 20–25 minutes, not nine minutes as the hotel states → use the free golf-cart shuttle to reach the main road and then call a Grab.

If a rooftop bar or on-site dining is important to you — Aladdin Rooftop Bar is no longer operating, and breakfast availability is inconsistent → verify what is actually running with the hotel before you book.

tips.title: Vejthani Hospital: 5 minutes by taxi
tips.body: Vejthani Hospital (Soi Lat Phrao 111) is 1.2 km away. A taxi from the hotel front takes under five minutes and typically costs 50–70 THB — the quickest, most comfortable option for patients and family.

tips.title: Clarify payment terms at check-in
tips.body: Some guests report an undisclosed credit card surcharge. Ask upfront about payment methods and any fees. The hotel takes a 500 THB refundable security deposit, returned at check-out.

tips.title: The Mall Bangkapi for meals and essentials
tips.body: The Mall Bangkapi is a few minutes by car and has restaurants, a food court, a supermarket, and pharmacies — convenient for medical visitors needing supplies between hospital visits.

faq.q: How far is Baron Zotel Bangkok from Vejthani Hospital?
faq.a: Baron Zotel Bangkok is on Soi Lat Phrao 117, approximately 1.2 km from Vejthani Hospital (Soi Lat Phrao 111). A taxi takes under five minutes and costs around 50–70 THB. Walking takes about 15 minutes. It is one of the closest budget hotels to Vejthani that maintains a strong review score.

faq.q: What is the price range at Baron Zotel Bangkok?
faq.a: Rooms start from about THB 500–650 per night for a Superior Room in regular periods, and THB 700–900 for a Deluxe Room (roughly USD 13–26 on international platforms). Prices vary by season and platform — comparing Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com before booking is worthwhile. A 500 THB refundable security deposit is taken at check-in.

faq.q: Does Baron Zotel Bangkok have free parking?
faq.a: Yes — free on-site parking is available for guests, making this a good option for anyone driving from outside Bangkok or renting a car for hospital visits · The hotel also offers a complimentary 24-hour golf-cart shuttle between the property and the main Lat Phrao road. Call ahead to confirm parking availability if you are arriving during a busy period.

faq.q: How far is the nearest MRT station from Baron Zotel Bangkok?
faq.a: The nearest station is Bang Kapi on the MRT Yellow Line (YL8), about 1.5 km away. The honest answer from real reviews is that the walking distance is closer to 20–25 minutes, not the nine minutes the hotel states. The practical solution: use the free golf-cart shuttle to Lat Phrao main road, then take a Grab to the station.

faq.q: Is the rooftop bar at Baron Zotel Bangkok still open?
faq.a: The Aladdin Rooftop Bar has appeared in the hotel's marketing, but multiple recent guest reviews confirm it is no longer operating. If on-site dining or a bar is important to your stay, contact the hotel directly before booking to confirm what is currently available.

faq.q: Is Baron Zotel Bangkok suitable for general tourists?
faq.a: The hotel is well-suited for medical visitors to Vejthani Hospital and for anyone working in the Bang Kapi and Lat Phrao area. For general tourists wanting to explore central Bangkok, the location requires long and relatively costly taxi or Grab rides to Sukhumvit, Siam, or the old city — in that case, a hotel closer to the BTS network in a central neighbourhood would serve you better.
